payload.title: docs/signals/ inbox carries a permanent ~54-file undeliverable floor — one class is live market intelligence that reaches nobody, and it saturates the drain's own MANDATORY PERSIST gate
payload.how_found: Router had reported a stable 54-file floor for three consecutive ticks WITHOUT ever inspecting what it consisted of. Treating a stable number as a healthy number was the error; this tick opened the files. Recording that explicitly so the lesson is not lost: a metric that never moves deserves inspection precisely BECAUSE it never moves.

finding_1_dead_market_detection_channel.severity: HIGH — market-facing data loss, currently live
finding_1_dead_market_detection_channel.what: Seven docs/signals/price_anomaly_*.json files (2026-07-02, 07-03, 07-04, 07-13, 07-16, 07-17, 07-21) are schema price_anomaly_v1 and carry NO 'from' and NO 'type' field. scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js therefore classifies each as 'SKIP non-signal shape ... leaving in inbox'. They have never been routed to PO, never fingerprinted into signals.db, and never consumed by anything. They simply accumulate.
finding_1_dead_market_detection_channel.why_it_matters: These are not junk or state dumps — they are the highest-quality market analysis in the inbox. Each carries per-ticker RSI, Bollinger-band position, volume-vs-21-day-average, 30-day return, MACD histogram direction, sector attribution, and individually-probed insider signals with an explicit statement that every 'no activity' value was probed rather than assumed. The 2026-07-21 file also self-documents its own data quality (yoy null rather than estimated; prices confirmed as EOD close not stale reads; chain corroboration explicitly absent).
finding_1_dead_market_detection_channel.the_convergence_that_makes_this_urgent: The 2026-07-21T16:13Z file describes EXACTLY the selloff alert-commander was silent on — GAS -6.98% (RSI 29.3, volume 4.0x average, below lower Bollinger band), BSR -6.49%, GEX -5.16% (RSI 19.9, the most extreme oversold reading, on 0.87x volume meaning no capitulation exhaustion yet), PLX -4.81%, FPT -3.43%, DIG -3.56%. That silence is the entire premise of DESIGN-COWORK-FANOUT-PRODUCER-CONSUMER-ORDERING, which was scoped as a producer/consumer ORDERING problem. This file shows the detection ALSO happened on a second, parallel plane and was structurally undeliverable regardless of ordering. PO should re-read the fan-out row in that light: fixing dispatch order alone would not have surfaced this analysis, because nothing consumes the file format it is written in.
finding_1_dead_market_detection_channel.also_carries_independent_corroboration_o: The file's own market_context.note reads: 'First EOD pass since 2026-07-17 — slot did not fire for 4 days (17th, 20th, 21st EOD gap; 18-19 weekend).' That is INDEPENDENT confirmation, from a different plane and a different author, of the market-watcher EOD slot-routing defect the architect root-caused today (market-watcher/flow/main.md routes on wall-clock windows and discards the slot= parameter, so a late-firing eod falls through to the generic offhours cycle and loses eod.md's ledger + signal deliverable). Two unrelated sources now agree the EOD slot is dropping days. The file-date gaps corroborate it a third time.
finding_1_dead_market_detection_channel.what_to_decide: Not merely 'add from/type to the writer'. Decide first WHERE this analysis is supposed to go. If price_anomaly_v1 is meant to reach PO/alert-commander, it needs the signal envelope and a routing-table row. If it is meant as a Chef/dish input read directly by path, then it does not belong in docs/signals/ at all and should live somewhere the drain does not police. What is not acceptable is the current state, where it looks delivered because it is in the inbox, and is not.

finding_2_saturated_mandatory_persist_ga.severity: MEDIUM — a guard that cannot fail
finding_2_saturated_mandatory_persist_ga.what: drain-signals.md line 7 (MANDATORY PERSIST GUARD) reads: 'ls docs/signals/*.json | wc -l -> if count > 50: full drain is REQUIRED this tick.' The undeliverable floor is ~54 files (44 cowork-team-*.json tick telemetry using emitted_by/emitted_at/classification rather than from/type, 7 price_anomaly_*, 3 misc-format cowork files). Because those files can never drain, the count can never fall below ~54, so the '> 50' predicate is TRUE on every tick forever.
finding_2_saturated_mandatory_persist_ga.why_it_matters: This is the same defect class as SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP is chartered to sweep for, and it is the FIFTH instance found this session across unrelated subsystems (the others: the tier-1 heartbeat freshness gate, which is DEAD rather than saturated, plus the three already on that row). The gate is not wrong today — a full drain genuinely was required this tick — but it is not MEASURING anything. If the real signal volume dropped to zero, the guard would still read REQUIRED. Any future reader who trusts it as evidence of inbox pressure will be misled.
finding_2_saturated_mandatory_persist_ga.note_on_the_44_telemetry_files: The cowork-team-*.json tick records are individually harmless and may be deliberate. Several are 11 days old (2026-07-10, 07-11). The question for PO is whether per-tick telemetry belongs in the same directory the drain treats as an inbox — that co-location is what produces the floor. If they are wanted, a sibling directory removes the floor without losing them.
finding_2_saturated_mandatory_persist_ga.suggested_fix_direction_not_prescribed: Either exclude non-signal-shaped files from the count so the predicate measures DRAINABLE backlog, or relocate telemetry out of the inbox. Router did not choose; both change the guard's meaning and that is a design call.
finding_2_saturated_mandatory_persist_ga.router_status: STILL VALID 2026-07-21T18:51:52Z — unaffected by the finding-1 retraction. Inbox has since grown 54 -> 59, so the >50 predicate is not merely saturated but has a monotonically RISING floor. Logged as confirmed_instance_1 on SPIKE-SATURATED-COUNT-THRESHOLD-GATES-SWEEP. Note the corrected fix direction: the count must exclude BOTH cowork telemetry AND the by-path price_anomaly_* family, which must never be swept — now written into CLEAN-COWORK-DISPATCHER-TELEMETRY-DRAIN-DIR acceptance (2)(3)(4).

payload.explicitly_not_claimed: Router did NOT locate the price_anomaly_v1 producer in source. grep across md/js/ts/sh found only documentation references and archived alert-commander notebooks, no writer. The file's own dish_window:'eod' field and its EOD-gap note point at a cowork EOD dish flow (market-watcher eod.md is the likely author given the R3 overlap), but that is INFERENCE, not verified attribution. Whoever works this row must confirm the writer at source before changing it.
payload.router_did_not_mint: Filed as a signal for PO triage rather than minted as a board row, per the standing rule that minting is PO's. PO is mid-cycle on a five-item decision batch at time of writing; this is deliberately queued behind that rather than interrupting it.
payload.SUPERSEDED_finding_1: ROUTER RETRACTION 2026-07-21T18:51:52Z — FINDING 1 IS FALSE. Router (author of this signal) filed it; PO disproved it at source and router independently re-verified both ends. price_anomaly_*.json ARE consumed. Writer: docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/eod.md:29 (Step B), output declared :13, contract stated :15 and :61 ("chef reads at 08:37 UTC, 24min settle window"). Consumer: docs/agents/unified-agent/flow/chef.md:116 — Chef reads them BY DIRECT PATH GLOB, not via the drain. The drain SKIP at scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js:100 ("leaving in inbox") is precisely what keeps them where Chef can see them. THE REQUESTED FIX WAS THE REGRESSION: adding from/type would make the drain MATCH and mv them to processed/, and chef.md:116 has NO processed/ dual-read (that AUTO-CURE covers bctc_signal_*/fundamental_* only), so the EOD dish would silently lose its market input. Do NOT act on finding 1. Replacement row: GUARD-PRICE-ANOMALY-BYPATH-DISH-CONTRACT (P1, agent-father, supervised).
payload.SUPERSEDED_why_four_agents_missed_it: ROOT CAUSE OF THE MIS-DIAGNOSIS, recorded because it will recur: every agent that searched for the writer (router included) excluded .md as "documentation" and grepped js/ts/sh only. In this system flow docs ARE the executable source for cowork agents, so a code-only writer search structurally CANNOT find any cowork writer. Empty result was then read as absence — the exact empty-read-is-not-evidence failure. Second contributor: docs/standards/mcp-tools.md:175 documents only the DB plane (post_agent_signal -> alert-commander, intraday); the file plane (eod.md -> Chef, EOD) is undocumented there, so the same name maps to two planes and only one is discoverable.
payload.cowork_dispatcher_composition_measuremen:
COWORK-DISPATCHER MEASUREMENT 2026-07-21T19:0xZ (tick 19:00Z, author = cowork-team dispatcher, i.e. the writer of the 51 telemetry files). Opening the files instead of counting them, per this signal's own how_found lesson.

COMPOSITION (floor now 59, was 54 @18:16Z): cowork-team telemetry 51, price_anomaly 7 (by-path, never sweep), misc 1.
Of the 51 telemetry files: 36 dated 2026-07-10, 7 dated 2026-07-11, 5 dated 2026-07-21, 3 misc-named.
==> 43/51 (84%) are a TWO-DAY BURST from 07-10/07-11, eleven days old. ZERO telemetry files exist for 07-12 through 07-20 (nine consecutive days).

SELF-CORRECTION: the dispatcher (me) wrote in its own prior tick analysis that "every 15-min tick makes this P1 worse". That OVERSTATES the ongoing rate and is corrected here. The dispatcher writes only on non-silent ticks, and only when a live CLI session exists (see project_cowork_guaranteed_slot_needs_live_cli_session) — so the long-run rate is ~0 on most days and bursty on active ones. The floor is NOT an ongoing drip; it is one historical burst that never got swept. Anyone sizing this fix off a per-tick growth rate will size it wrong.

THE FIX IS ALREADY DESIGNED AND 9 DAYS STALE — this is recurring-failed-fix, not a new finding. docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-12-ultracode-workflow-improvement-audit.md:675 already specifies a retention sweep of docs/signals/cowork-team-*.json inside a new scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-postflight.sh, ">14 days -> delete", via `git rm` with explicit pathspec. Same brief already counted this floor at lines 651 and 1087 (45 then 48 files). It was never implemented.

THE DESIGNED THRESHOLD DOES NOT FIX THE CURRENT SATURATION. The saturating files are 11 days old; a >14-day sweep first catches them on 2026-07-25. Implementing the retention rule exactly as designed leaves the >50 gate saturated for four more days. Whoever implements CLEAN-COWORK-DISPATCHER-TELEMETRY-DRAIN-DIR must either shorten the window or make the sweep count-aware, not just age-aware.

MECHANICS CONFIRMED STILL TRUE: all 43 burst files are git-tracked (verified by git ls-files per file; tracked=43 untracked=0), so `git rm` with explicit pathspec is correct and a plain rm would leave a dirty tree. Removing exactly those 43 drops the floor 59 -> 16, restoring the >50 predicate immediately, touching ZERO price_anomaly files.

NO CONSUMER — re-verified with a working positive control. Every path-level reference to docs/signals/cowork-team-* across js/ts/sh/md is a writer (telemetry.md:34, telemetry.md:104, match-slots.md:32), a prose mention, or an audit counting them. No reader. Control: the identical query against price_anomaly returns its known live consumer set, so the empty reader-result is a real absence, not a broken query. (First attempt at this grep silently matched nothing due to unquoted zsh globs on --include; the positive control failed identically, which is what exposed it.)

NEW DEFECT, LOW SEVERITY, EVIDENCE DELIBERATELY PRESERVED: docs/signals/cowork-team-20260721T183028Z.json is ZERO BYTES, untracked, written 18:30:28Z — 21 seconds before the successful 18:30:49Z write of the same tick. The telemetry write path can therefore emit an empty artifact without erroring or being noticed. NOT deleted: a 0-byte file's forensic content IS its existence, so removing it as garbage would destroy the only evidence of the defect. Whoever implements the sweep should treat it as a finding first and debris second.
